rule: Always decouple stamina drain from frame rates by multiplying delta time into the depletion formula.
Never run line-of-sight visibility traces on every tick for off-screen entities; use an interval throttled timer.

Never generate flat, boring top-down tile grids or simple single-room box layouts. For 2.5D or perspective games, mandate dynamic pseudo-3D perspective projection, multi-layered background parallax, Y-sorting for depth layering, and visually distinct environmental geometry.

Every action-RPG or combat-focused prototype must feature responsive hitbox detection, particle or screen-space feedback on impact, enemy health bars, and an active combat loop rather than static placeholder boxes.

Never rely on minimalist floating text labels as a substitute for a polished HUD. Canvas prototypes must render atmospheric borders, stylized health/stamina meters, and clear, styled typography matching the game's setting.
Mandate proper isometric projection formulas (screenX = (x - y) * (tileWidth / 2) + centerX, screenY = (x + y) * (tileHeight / 2) + centerY) for all 2.5D spatial positioning.

Never draw entities in a static order. All environmental structures, actors, and items must be pushed into a unified render array and sorted by their calculated screen vertical position (item.y) before drawing.
Implement an input buffer queue for combat actions to prevent dropped key presses during attack animations and state transitions.
Never instantiate dynamic particle or projectile objects inside the render/update tick loop; utilize a pre-allocated object pool to eliminate garbage collection stutters.
Enforce explicit finite state machine (FSM) rules for actors and enemies to cleanly handle interruption states (stun, dodge, death) without input deadlocks.
When generating procedural environments or rooms, utilize seeded cellular automata or BSP tree partitioning rather than random noise to guarantee traversable corridors and connected layouts.
For entity-dense simulations, implement a spatial hash grid or quadtree structure for collision queries to avoid costly $O(N^2)$ pairwise checks during the update loop.
Programmatically synthesize sound effects and ambient feedback utilizing the Web Audio API (oscillators, gain nodes, custom envelope ramps) to maintain self-contained, asset-free execution.
For multiplayer or simulated co-op systems, separate deterministic game logic state updates entirely from rendering presentation layers to support future lockstep synchronization.
Use modular steering behaviors (seek, flee, arrive, separation) and weighted behavior trees for non-player characters to produce organic, non-linear group movement.
